title: The Sparrow’s Gifts
place: A village beside a bamboo grove
note: A gentler, shortened adaptation of “The Tongue-Cut Sparrow.” The source includes cruelty to the sparrow; this version states the harm without dwelling on it.

rights.basis: Source edition published before 1929 and identified as public domain by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A sparrow waits in a bamboo grove beside two woven baskets.
scenes: An old woodcutter cared for a little sparrow. While he worked, a bad-tempered neighbor punished the bird for eating her rice paste and drove it away.
The woodcutter searched through fields and bamboo, calling until the sparrow answered. Its family welcomed him to a beautiful house hidden in the grove.
After food, music, and many thanks, the sparrows offered two baskets: one large and one small. The tired woodcutter chose the small basket and carried it home.
Inside were coins and treasures. Hearing this, the greedy neighbor hurried to the grove, demanded the largest basket, and ignored the warning not to open it before reaching home.
On the road she lifted the lid. Startling creatures and shadows flew out, and she fled, leaving the basket behind.
The woodcutter shared his good fortune. The sparrows’ gifts had revealed what each visitor already carried inside.
